summary: Penobscot County lookout: 1910 station, a steel tower finished in 1918. The FFLA lists the steel still standing with its cab no longer in place.

facts.design: Steel lookout tower; its cab is no longer in place
facts.status_note: The steel tower still stands, but its cab is no longer in place (FFLA).

events.note: Station built on Ragged Mountain, equipped with instruments and a cooking outfit
Cabin burned in early spring, cause unknown; a new 12 x 14 cabin was built
Steel tower completed in 1918, after a 36-foot tower was partly erected in 1917

evidence.supports: 1910 station built, equipped with instruments and cooking outfit
evidence.quote: New lookout station was constructed on Ragged Mountain, completely equipped with instruments, cooking outfit, etc.

evidence.supports: 1916 cabin burned, cause unknown, presumed fishermen or hunters
evidence.quote: The cabin on Ragged Mountain was burned during the early spring, cause unknown
presume it was fishermen or hunters, leaving a fire in the small stove
A new cabin, 12 x 14 was built.
A 36-foot ste el tower was partly erected

evidence.supports: 1919 panoramic map centred on the tower, Township 4, Indian Purchase
evidence.quote: 360 degree panoramic map centered on the Ragged Mt. fire tower located in Township 4, Indian Purchase, ME, 1919.

evidence.supports: FFLA list: Ragged Mountain, Penobscot, Tower Standing*
asterisk marks towers whose cab is no longer in place
evidence.quote: Towers that retain their structure and support with the cab no longer in place

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1917 entry gives a 36-foot tower partly erected; the 1920 inventory lists 48 feet. The record's 11.0 m matches the 36-foot figure. The later 48-foot (14.6 m) figure is used here; the editor should decide.

sources.title: Ragged Mt. 1919 (Fire Tower Maps, Maine Forest Service)
sources.publisher: Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (digitalmaine.com)

notes_for_editor: Access, ownership and the date the cab came down are not in any source reached. No trail or visitor source found for this Penobscot County mountain; the search returned a different Ragged Mountain in Knox County (Camden/Rockport), which is not this tower and was not used. Height conflict: the record's 11.0 m matches the 1917 36-foot figure; the 1920 inventory says 48 feet. Visit and access keys omitted until confirmed.
